title: Can quicksand kill you?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore whether quicksand can kill you. They open with Gilligan's Island and movie/TV quicksand clichés, then cover a 2005 Nature study finding a human cannot sink in quicksand and die (buoyancy, density about twice water), the science of reology, how quicksand forms (upward water flow from springs, earthquakes, saturation), why struggling makes sinking worse, the advice to wriggle out and float on your back, and dry quicksand created in a lab. They survey quicksand in film and TV (via quicksandmovies.net), including The Acid Eaters, Operation Silent Night on Magnum P.I., and The Simpsons. The episode closes with a listener mail segment answering Facebook questions about prep, college majors, pet peeves and more.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Facebook questions

segments.title: Opening banter and Gilligan's Island
segments.summary: Hosts banter and joke about Gilligan's Island quicksand episodes and quicksand as a movie device, then introduce the question of whether quicksand can kill you.

segments.title: Can quicksand kill you? The 2005 study
segments.summary: They cite a 2005 study concluding a person cannot physically sink into quicksand and die. Human body density is about one gram per cubic centimeter while quicksand is about twice that, so a person floats. Quicksand is solid ground liquefied by saturation, and the field of reology is introduced.

segments.title: How quicksand forms
segments.summary: Quicksand forms mainly from upward movement of water from springs or from earthquakes loosening ground and adding water. The hosts compare it to a sinkhole and relate it to geology.

segments.title: Why quicksand traps you and how to get out
segments.summary: Water breaks the friction between sand grains, so the sand loses stability. Pulling out quickly requires huge force, and struggling makes sinking worse. The advice is to move slowly, wriggle, and lean back to float. Friends should not pull with a vine. A bear escaping quicksand video is mentioned.

segments.title: Dry quicksand and lab experiments
segments.summary: Dry quicksand, a loose sand arrangement that has only been created in a lab and not observed in nature, is discussed. It could be deadly if deep enough because there is no water to provide buoyancy. The Dune sandworm reference is made.

segments.title: Quicksand in film and TV
segments.summary: Hosts list quicksand scenes drawn from quicksandmovies.net, including The Acid Eaters, Magnum P.I.'s Operation Silent Night, General Hospital, Benny Hill, Fantasy Island, Dynasty, G.I. Joe, Creep Show, and The Simpsons.

segments.title: Closing recommendations
segments.summary: Hosts recommend the How Stuff Works quicksand article and a Discovery Channel-style animation, then mention the Worst Case Scenario handbook.

segments.title: Listener mail from Facebook
segments.summary: Hosts answer Facebook questions about recording prep, college majors (both attended University of Georgia), pet peeves, podcast ideas, high school, and soup versus chowder (geography, not cooking difference).
